channel.title: Threat Desk
channel.description: Vulnerabilities, advisories and threat activity, twice a day

item.title: Signal blocks OS AI agents from reading chats
item.description: Signal has implemented platform-specific measures to prevent iOS and Android AI agents from accessing user messages, citing a lack of control over data collection by operating system features.

item.title: Police disrupt 57 illegal streaming services in 11-country operation
item.description: Law enforcement from 11 countries disrupted 57 illegal IPTV services, identifying 321 websites and tracing over €26 million in cryptocurrency transactions.

item.title: ShinyHunters claims return via new Tor site after member arrests
item.description: The extortion group has relaunched its data leak site, using historical PGP keys to assert legitimacy following a series of international arrests targeting its members.

item.title: Unclassified CIA system breached in cyberattack, AP source says
item.description: A person familiar with the incident told the Associated Press that an unclassified CIA system handling open-source intelligence was compromised, though no classified data was accessed.

item.title: Attackers use stolen AI prompt credentials to probe AWS infrastructure
item.description: Security firm Dragos traced AWS API calls to credentials planted in AI prompts, revealing that attackers are harvesting secrets from AI hosting providers.

item.title: NCSC issues guidance to counter agentic offensive frameworks
item.description: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre has published an eight-point plan to help defenders mitigate the surge in automated attacks from agentic offensive frameworks.

item.title: Drupal RCE flaw CVE-2026-132165 actively exploited
item.description: CISA has added a critical Drupal vulnerability to its KEV Catalog after confirming active exploitation that allows site takeover via the installer.

item.title: Turnitin investigating unauthorised activity on customer-facing systems
item.description: Education technology firm Turnitin has disclosed unauthorised activity on certain customer-facing systems, with the University of Colorado Boulder monitoring its integration.

item.title: NCC Group: Ransomware claims rise 23% in October
item.description: A new report indicates a sharp increase in claimed ransomware incidents, driven by AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and the emergence of new extortion brands.

item.title: Fake WordPress plugin bypasses 2FA and serves malicious scripts
item.description: Wordfence identified a hidden plugin that creates valid login sessions without 2FA and relays attacker-controlled JavaScript to visitors.

item.title: New gang Inception denies ShinyHunters rebranding claims
item.description: Security researchers have theorised that the data theft and extortion group Inception is a rebrand of ShinyHunters, a claim the new crew has explicitly rejected.

item.title: US Treasury's FinCEN takes systems offline after cyber incident
item.description: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network has disconnected some systems to investigate unauthorised access, causing temporary service disruptions and filing deadline extensions.

item.title: Ransomware hits Port of Santos and Argentinian pipeline
item.description: Industrial sectors in Latin America face a surge in ransomware, with recent attacks affecting major infrastructure in Brazil and Argentina.

item.title: Aikido finds 42 phishing pages on Hugging Face
item.description: Attackers used Hugging Face's DeepSite AI to create fake login pages for 28 brands, including Microsoft and Google, to harvest credentials.

item.title: ShinyHunters alleged return claimed as Inception denies ties
item.description: A new extortion group called Inception has emerged, while someone claiming to represent ShinyHunters has announced the group’s alleged return, prompting denial from Inception operators.

item.title: Adobe patches critical flaws in Experience Manager and Campaign Classic
item.description: Adobe released updates on 24 November 2026 to fix critical vulnerabilities in Experience Manager and Campaign Classic that allow code execution and privilege escalation.

item.title: InfraTrust: Exploited supply chain flaws dominate recent advisories
item.description: Eclypsium's November report highlights that most critical infrastructure vulnerabilities are in bundled third-party software, creating patching delays for enterprises.

item.title: Todoist breach exposes user data and integration tokens
item.description: An attacker accessed Todoist production systems via stolen credentials, exfiltrating account records for roughly 6% of users and compromising Outlook mailbox data.

item.title: Microsoft: Salt Typhoon and Crystal Typhoon using Artex AI tool
item.description: Microsoft reported that Chinese state-backed groups are using the Artex AI platform to automate network reconnaissance and exploitation at machine speed.

item.title: Roundcube Webmail patches 12 flaws in 1.6.22 and 1.7.7
item.description: Roundcube released updates on 23 November 2026 to fix 12 security vulnerabilities, including issues with attachment handling and unencrypted connections.

item.title: Microsoft warns state-backed groups use ARTEX AI agents for rapid intrusions
item.description: Microsoft identified six threat actors, including Storm-0940, using the ARTEX framework to automate credential theft and privileged access in cloud environments.

item.title: Iranian group Volant Manticore targets Cypriot organisations
item.description: A previously undocumented Iranian threat group is conducting espionage against Cypriot entities to gather intelligence for Tehran.

item.title: FIFA confirms breach; HBHC claims 12.2 GB data leak
item.description: FIFA has confirmed unauthorised access to personal and business data, though it has not verified the Handsome Boy Hacking Club's claim of a 12.2 GB archive.

item.title: CIA OSINT system reportedly breached; FinCEN takes systems offline
item.description: Unknown attackers reportedly used the ARTEX AI framework to breach an unclassified CIA system, while FinCEN disclosed a separate incident prompting precautionary system shutdowns.

item.title: Switzerland confirms first AI-agent cyberattacks on critical infrastructure
item.description: Swiss and Italian agencies report successful intrusions using autonomous AI agents, urging immediate patching of internet-facing systems.

item.title: 1Password breach exposes customer data via compromised GitHub account
item.description: 1Password disclosed that an attacker accessed backend systems through a hijacked employee GitHub account, stealing customer names and emails, though vault contents remained secure.

item.title: Cisco UCS UEFI Shell flaw allows Secure Boot bypass
item.description: Cisco has released fixes for a high-severity vulnerability in UCS servers and appliances that permits attackers to bypass UEFI Secure Boot validation.

item.title: Ghostscript sandbox escape enables RCE via crafted file uploads
item.description: Security firm pwn.ai demonstrated that a now-patched Ghostscript flaw allows crafted file uploads to escape the sandbox and execute remote code on Linux servers.

item.title: OpenRouter removes three providers after prompt theft
item.description: Researchers at Dragos discovered that attackers stole data from three AI inference providers for months, including requests marked as Zero Data Retention.

item.title: Bulgaria reveals five-year government data breach
item.description: Bulgarian authorities discovered a cyberespionage campaign active since 2021 that exfiltrated 130 GB of sensitive state documents, highlighting critical gaps in national security monitoring.
